history.content: who contributed more to the design of skyscrapers

Chicago architects and the Beaux-Arts movement contributed significantly to the design of skyscrapers. Chicago architects, including William Le Baron Jenney, Louis Sullivan, and John Root, developed a new architectural style known as the "Chicago School of Architecture." This style combined aesthetic theory with practical commercial sense, featuring rich, ornate designs at the ground level and simpler ornamentation on the upper levels. They also emphasized strong vertical lines and comprehensible roof structures to draw the observer's eye upward. On the other hand, the Beaux-Arts movement, along with advocates of the Exposition in Chicago, proposed low-rise cities with wide boulevards and a unified design called "horizontal visual unity." This approach aimed for each building to have unique features while elegantly complementing its neighbors, typically by being built to a common height. However, critics from this movement, such as Montgomery Schuyler and Charles Lamb, condemned the skyscrapers in New York for creating a "horribly jagged sierra" city skyline and impinging on the rights of the rest of the city, respectively. Some architects, like Charles McKim and Stanford White, even refused to work on skyscraper projects.
How Chicago became the pioneer of skyscraper designs?

Chicago became the pioneer of skyscraper designs due to several reasons. Firstly, during the late 1880s and early 1890s, many skyscrapers were constructed in the center of Chicago's financial district, making it a hub for skyscraper innovation. These skyscrapers, sometimes referred to as the products of the "Chicago School of Architecture," aimed to balance aesthetic concerns with practical commercial design. 
They featured large, square, palazzo-styled buildings with shops and restaurants on the ground level and rentable offices on the upper floors. Secondly, Chicago architects, such as William Le Baron Jenney, Louis Sullivan, and John Root, developed a unique architectural style that combined aesthetic theory with practical commercial sense. This style emphasized rich, ornate designs at the ground level and simpler ornamentation on the upper levels, with strong vertical lines and comprehensible roof structures. 
These features helped draw the observer's eye upward and celebrate the "lofty" nature of the skyscraper while also making the building stand out to passers-by and attracting necessary business for a successful commercial building. In contrast, New York's skyscrapers were frequently narrower towers that were more eclectic in style and often criticized for their lack of elegance. In 1892, Chicago even banned the construction of new skyscrapers taller than 150 feet (46 m), leaving the development of taller buildings to New York. All these factors contributed to Chicago's reputation as a pioneer in skyscraper design.
What is Beaux art style also known as?

The Beaux-Arts style is also known as the French Beaux-Arts movement or the Italian Renaissance style, originating from the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris. It is characterized by applying Classical aesthetic principles to modern buildings.
I thought it originated in Chicago?

I apologize for any confusion. While the Beaux-Arts movement did influence American architects, including those in Chicago, the movement itself originated in France at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris. American architects who studied there brought these ideals and standards back to the United States in the 1880s.
And who among them pioneered the world's first skyscraper, can you refresh my memory?

The world's first skyscraper, the Home Insurance Building, was designed by William Le Baron Jenney. He was a leading architect in Chicago and had been trained as an engineer in France. This 138-foot 10-story skyscraper was notable for incorporating structural steel into its internal metal frame, which supported the floors and helped carry the weight of the external walls. This design was an essential step towards the development of non-structural curtain walls in later skyscrapers. This engineering innovation established Chicago from that time on to become one of the world's most influential epicenters of contemporary urban and commercial architecture.

evidence.text: The social and economic reasons for the appearance of the blues are not fully known . Blues has evolved from an unaccompanied vocal music of poor black laborers into a wide variety of styles and subgenres , with regional variations across the United States . African American work songs were an important precursor to the modern blues ; these included the songs sung by laborers like stevedores and roustabouts , and the field hollers and `` shouts '' of slaves . The first appearance of the blues is not well defined and is often dated between 1870 and 1900 , a period that coincides with the emancipation of the slaves and the transition from slavery to sharecropping and small - scale agricultural production in the southern United States .
